title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: PLAC — God imputes when crime also lives in descendants
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: if God imputes parents' crime to the unborn and to grandsons, it is because that crime also has place in them as they imitate or approve ancestors' traditions and manners. So Jeroboam's sin remained in the ten tribes after his death, and the Jews who crucified the Lord of glory have posterity who still approve and foster that sin in themselves.
pass_b_english: PLAC. If parents' crime is imputed by God to those yet to be born and to grandsons, that is done because that crime also has place in those yet to be born and in grandsons, imitating or approving the traditions and manners of their ancestors. So Jeroboam's sin, he being dead, remained in the ten tribes, and the sin of the Jews who crucified the Lord of glory their posterity today approve, and foster and conserve in themselves.
source_text: PLAC. Si parentum crimen nascituris & nepotibus imputatur a Deo, id fit, quia illud crimen in nascituris & nepotibus etiam locum habet, maiorum traditiones & mores imitantibus, aut probantibus. Sic peccatum Jeroboami, eo mortuo, in decem tribubus permansit, & peccatum Judaeorum, qui Dominum gloriae crucifixerunt, eorum posteri hodie probant, & in seipsis fovent ac conservant.

choices.choice: God imputes when descendants imitate/approve ancestors' crime
